prompt.context: Our client is an upscale restaurant in Tianjin, serving government officials and high-level business customers. Its monthly revenue is 1.2 million Yuan. The CEO recently hired McKinsey to help them increase profits. As China's economy is booming, the upscale dining market is growing at 20% every year. Customers for high-end dining are generally price insensitive. All competitors are earning money. Competitors' price and value proposition are similar. Variable costs across the industry are 50% of revenue. Assume no fixed costs. On weekdays, there is always a line for individual rooms. As a result, the restaurant has to turn away half of its customers due to capacity constraint.
prompt.question: How can the client increase profits?

clarifying_info.q: What types of seating does the restaurant have?
clarifying_info.a: The restaurant has two types of rooms: Individual Rooms (20 tables) and Big Rooms (20 tables). Government officials and business customers prefer individual rooms due to privacy requirements.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current occupancy and pricing by room type and meal period?
clarifying_info.a: Individual Rooms (20 tables): Weekday Lunch - 80% occupancy, 150 Yuan/person, 4 per table; Weekday Dinner - 100% occupancy, 300 Yuan/person, 6 per table; Weekend Lunch - 30% occupancy, 100 Yuan/person, 4 per table; Weekend Dinner - 50% occupancy, 200 Yuan/person, 6 per table. Big Rooms (20 tables): Weekday Lunch - 20% occupancy, 100 Yuan/person, 4 per table; Weekday Dinner - 30% occupancy, 200 Yuan/person, 4 per table; Weekend Lunch - 30% occupancy, 100 Yuan/person, 4 per table; Weekend Dinner - 30% occupancy, 200 Yuan/person, 4 per table.

framework: Diagnose current profitability: understand revenue, costs, and profit structure by room type and time period
Identify root cause of low profits: assess demand vs. capacity mismatch, especially for individual rooms
Generate solutions: pricing optimization and/or capacity reallocation
Evaluate feasibility and total cost (including opportunity costs) of capacity changes

questions.prompt: What is the reason for the client's low profits?
questions.guidance: The key insight is that the restaurant is not meeting customer demand for individual rooms. On weekdays, individual rooms are at or near full capacity (100% dinner, 80% lunch) and the restaurant turns away half its customers. Big rooms have much lower occupancy. The client is supply-constrained for the higher-value individual rooms while big room capacity sits underutilized.

questions.prompt: What are potential solutions to increase profitability?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should identify at least two levers: (1) Raise prices for individual rooms — customers are price insensitive and demand exceeds supply, especially for weekday dinner where underlying demand is 200% of capacity; (2) Convert big room tables into individual rooms to capture unmet demand.

questions.prompt: Market research shows that raising the weekday individual room price by 33% will cause a 10% customer loss. How will this change profitability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the incremental profit for both weekday lunch and weekday dinner separately, then sum. Key insight: for weekday dinner, since underlying demand is 200% of current capacity, raising price will NOT reduce volume — the restaurant is already turning customers away. Only lunch sees a volume reduction.

math.setup: Calculate incremental profit for weekday lunch and weekday dinner in individual rooms after a 33% price increase with 10% customer loss at lunch.
steps: Weekday Lunch — Previous: Customers = 4 x 20 x 80% = 64; Price = 150; Revenue = 64 x 150 = 9,600; Profit = 9,600 x 50% = 4,800
Weekday Lunch — Now: Customers = 64 x (1 - 10%) = 58 (approx); Price = 150 x (1 + 33%) = 200; Revenue = 58 x 200 = 11,600; Profit = 11,600 x 50% = 5,800
Weekday Dinner — Previous: Customers = 6 x 20 x 100% = 120; Price = 300; Revenue = 120 x 300 = 36,000; Profit = 36,000 x 50% = 18,000
Weekday Dinner — Now: Customers = 120 (no volume loss; demand is 200% of capacity); Price = 300 x (1 + 33%) = 400; Revenue = 120 x 400 = 48,000; Profit = 48,000 x 50% = 24,000
math.answer: Daily incremental profit from the 33% price increase = 7,000 Yuan

questions.prompt: A second solution is converting half of the big room tables into 5 individual rooms. Decoration takes 2 weeks and the restaurant must shut down completely. Decoration costs 100K Yuan. What is the total cost of this project?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify two cost components: (1) capital investment for decoration, and (2) opportunity cost from the 2-week shutdown. A strong candidate will use the monthly revenue figure given at the start (1.2M Yuan/month) to quickly estimate the opportunity cost, rather than reconstructing it from the detailed table. Monthly revenue = 1.2M, so 2 weeks ≈ 0.6M; profit margin = 50%, so opportunity cost ≈ 300K Yuan.

math.setup: Total cost = capital investment + opportunity cost of 2-week shutdown.
steps: Monthly revenue = 1,200,000 Yuan; 2 weeks ≈ half a month = 600,000 Yuan revenue foregone
math.answer: Total cost of the conversion project = 400,000 Yuan

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential solutions for the situation where the restaurant cannot meet customer demand for individual rooms?

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Raise individual room prices to manage excess demand and increase margin
Implement dynamic/surge pricing on weekday evenings
Introduce a premium reservation fee for individual rooms

categories.name: Capacity reallocation
ideas: Convert big room tables into individual rooms
Convert a portion of big room space into additional individual rooms
Explore physical expansion if adjacent space is available

categories.name: Operational efficiency
ideas: Reduce table turnover time to serve more customers per day
Increase sittings per day (add additional lunch/dinner service)
Optimize room booking process to minimize no-shows

recommendation: Pursue both solutions: raise weekday individual room prices by 33% immediately (no capital outlay, 7K Yuan daily incremental profit) and convert 10 big room tables into 5 individual rooms to capture structural demand
The price increase is low-risk given price-insensitive customers and excess demand at dinner; the capacity conversion addresses the root constraint
risks: 2-week full shutdown for renovation creates ~300K Yuan opportunity cost
If the conversion underperforms (individual rooms not fully adopted), ROI timeline extends
Raising prices could set a precedent that competitors follow, escalating price competition
next_steps: Conduct detailed financial modeling to validate renovation ROI payback period
Plan the renovation timeline to minimize disruption (e.g., schedule during a low-season period)
Monitor customer retention after price increase before committing to renovation
